card.name: Have before idea, faith, knowledge
card.fires_on: The verb have, or the quantifier right after it (no, much, any), when a person has or lacks an idea, knowledge, a clue or faith. The subject is usually I, many people or readers.

modes.label: No idea
modes.description: The word no after have, in the phrase have no idea or have no real idea.
modes.example: many consumers have<< no>> idea what British Colonial style is, or

modes.label: Have after a person
modes.description: The verb have after a person subject, before something known, seen or possessed such as a clue, examples or an object seen.
modes.example: anyone who might<< have>> a clue as to the nature of these

modes.label: Quantifier after have
modes.description: A quantifier such as much or any right after have, before faith or knowledge.
modes.example: I have<< much>> more faith in our public-school system than

card.writes: It pushes toward nouns of mental attitude such as confidence, interest, courage and ability, and away from verbs of knowing or having.
card.plain: It fires on "have" or "no" when someone is said to have an idea, a clue or some faith or knowledge.
